amendments.name: Amendment a
amendments.summary: An exclusion criterion for patients with retinopathy or maculopathy was added due to the potential risk of fundal hemorrhage induced by hypoglycemia. The GlucaGen reconstitution volume was changed from 1.0 mL to 1.1 mL in accordance with instructions in the Summary of Product Characteristics (2015).

changes.name: Section 6.2 Exclusion Criteria
changes.summary: [36] have preproliferative and proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy requiring treatment or not clinically stable in the last 6 months, or patients with active changes in subjective eye symptoms as determined by the investigator if an eye exam has not been performed in the last 6 months. Note: If an eye examination has been performed no more than 6 months before screening, it will not have to be repeated; however, the investigator will need to confirm via interview that there is no change in subjective symptoms.
changes.rationale: An exclusion criterion for patients with retinopathy or maculopathy was added due to the potential risk of fundal hemorrhage induced by hypoglycemia.

changes.name: Section 9.2.2.2 Intramuscular Glucagon Administration
changes.summary: GlucaGen 1 mg for injection will be used as a comparator. The lyophilized 1 mg glucagon will be reconstituted with 1.01.1 mL diluent according to the instruction.
changes.rationale: The GlucaGen reconstitution volume was changed from 1.0 mL to 1.1 mL in accordance with instructions in the Summary of Product Characteristics (2015).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Diabetes diagnosis and insulin therapy
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have had a diagnosis of either: [1a] T1DM based on the World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria, and have been on the following daily insulin therapy for at least 1 year: [A] multiple daily injection of long-acting insulin analog (either insulin glargine [U-100 or U-300] or insulin degludec [U-100]) and rapid-acting insulin analog (insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine), or [B] continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII); Or [1b] T2DM based on the WHO diagnostic criteria, and have received the following daily insulin therapy with or without oral anti-hyperglycemic medications (OAMs) for at least 1 year: [A] insulin: long-acting insulin analog (either insulin glargine [U-100 or U-300] or insulin degludec [U-100]) alone, or in combination with rapid-acting insulin analog (insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine) or CSII; [B] OAM: up to 3 of the following OAMs in accordance with local regulations: metformin, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, sodium glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, sulfonylurea (should not be more than half of maximum approved doses), glinides, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, or thiazolidine

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Male contraception agreement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: male patients: agree to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 28 days following the last study treatment

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Female contraception and pregnancy requirements
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: female patients: [3a] women of childbearing potential who are abstinent (if this is complete abstinence, as their preferred and usual lifestyle) or in a same sex relationship (as part of their preferred and usual lifestyle) must agree to either remain abstinent or stay in a same sex relationship without sexual relationships with males. Periodic abstinence (eg, calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post-ovulation methods), declaration of abstinence just for the duration of a trial, and withdrawal are not acceptable methods of contraception. [3b] otherwise, women of childbearing potential participating must agree to use one highly effective method (less than 1% failure rate) of contraception, or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception for the entirety of the study. [A] women of childbearing potential participating must test negative for pregnancy prior to initiation of treatment as indicated by a negative serum pregnancy test at the screening visit followed by a negative urine pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to exposure. [B] either one highly effective method of contraception or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception will be used. The patient may choose to use a double barrier method of contraception. Barrier protection methods without concomitant use of a spermicide are not a reliable or acceptable method. Thus, each barrier method must include use of a spermicide. It should be noted that the use of male and female condoms as a double barrier method is not considered acceptable due to the high failure rate when these methods are combined. [3c] women not of childbearing potential may participate, and include those who are: [A] infertile due to surgical sterilization (hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, or tubal ligation), congenital anomaly such as mullerian agenesis; Or [B] postmenopausal, defined as either: [i] a woman at least 50 years of age with an intact uterus, not on hormone therapy, who has had either: [a] cessation of menses for at least 1 year, or [b] at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea with a follicle-stimulating hormone >40 mIU/mL; or [ii] a woman 55 or older not on hormone therapy, who has had at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea, or [iii] a woman at least 55 years of age with a diagnosis of menopause prior to starting hormone replacement therapy

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Age range
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are between 18 and 64 years old for T1DM, or between 20 and 70 years old for T2DM at the time of informed consent

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Body mass index
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a body mass index of 18.5 to 30.0 kg/m2 for T1DM, or 18.5 to 35.0 kg/m2 for T2DM at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: HbA1c value
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a hemoglobin A1c value ≤10% at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Clinical laboratory test results
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have clinical laboratory test results within normal reference range (except for glycemic parameters) for the population or investigative site, or results with acceptable deviations that are judged to be not clinically significant by the investigator

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Venous access
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have venous access sufficient to allow for blood sampling and administration of insulin for IV administration as per the protocol

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Reliability and availability
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are reliable and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and are willing to follow study procedures

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Informed consent
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are able and willing to give signed informed consent

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Investigative site personnel exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are investigative site personnel directly affiliated with this study and their immediate families. Immediate family is defined as a spouse, biological or legal guardian, child, or sibling

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Lilly employees exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are Lilly employees

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Current clinical trial enrollment exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are currently enrolled in a clinical trial involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent investigational product participation exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have participated, within the last 4 months, in a clinical trial involving an investigational product. If the previous investigational product has a long half-life, 4 months or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) should have passed from the last dose of investigational product

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior LY900018 study participation exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have previously completed or withdrawn from this study or any other study investigating LY900018, and have previously received LY900018

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Known allergies or sensitivity exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have known allergies or sensitivity to LY900018, glucagon, related compounds, or any components of the formulation, or history of significant atopy

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Abnormal ECG exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have an abnormality in the 12-lead ECG that, in the opinion of the investigator, increases the risks associated with participating in the study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Unstable insulin regimen or blood glucose control exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: any significant changes in insulin regimen and/or unstable blood glucose control within the past 3 months prior to screening as assessed by the investigator

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: High total daily insulin dose exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have received a total daily dose of insulin >1.2 U/kg at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Poorly controlled hypertension exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have poorly controlled hypertension (ie, supine systolic BP >165 mm Hg or supine diastolic BP >95 mm Hg) at screening, or a change in antihypertensive medications within 30 days prior to screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Pheochromocytoma or insulinoma history exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of pheochromocytoma (ie, adrenal gland tumor) or insulinoma

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Severe hypoglycemia or loss of consciousness history exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of an episode of severe hypoglycemia (as defined by an episode that required third party assistance for treatment) in the 1 month prior to screening or have a history of loss of consciousness within the last 2 years induced other than by hypoglycemia

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Epilepsy or seizure disorder exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of epilepsy or seizure disorder

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Significant medical disorders exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history or presence of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine (apart from T1DM or T2DM), hematological, or neurological disorders capable of significantly altering the absorption, metabolism, or elimination of drugs; of constituting a risk when taking the investigational product; or of interfering with the interpretation of data

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Psychiatric disorders exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have known or ongoing psychiatric disorders that, in the opinion of the investigator, may preclude the patient from following and completing the protocol

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Drug abuse exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: regularly use known drugs of abuse and/or show positive findings on urinary drug screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: HIV infection exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and/or positive HIV antibodies and/or antigen

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatitis C exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of hepatitis C and/or positive hepatitis C antibody

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatitis B exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of hepatitis B and/or positive hepatitis B surface antigen

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Syphilis exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of syphilis and/or are positive for syphilis test

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Lactating women exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are women who are lactating

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prohibited medications exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: use of daily systemic beta-blocker, indomethacin, warfarin, anticholinergic drugs

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Blood donation exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have donated 400 mL or more blood in the last 12 weeks (males) or in the last 16 weeks (females), or any blood donation (including apheresis) within the last 4 weeks, or total volume of blood donation within 12 months is 1200 mL (males)/800 mL (females) or more at screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Excessive alcohol intake exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have an average weekly alcohol intake that exceeds 21 units per week (males up to age 65) and 14 units per week (males over 65 and females), or are unwilling to stop alcohol consumption from Day -2 to discharge from CRU in each period (1 unit = 12 oz or 360 mL of beer; 5 oz or 150 mL of wine; 1.5 oz or 45 mL of distilled spirits)

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Investigator or sponsor unsuitability exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: in the opinion of the investigator or sponsor, are unsuitable for inclusion in the study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Retinopathy or maculopathy exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have pre-proliferative and proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy requiring treatment or not clinically stable in the last 6 months, or patients with active changes in subjective eye symptoms as determined by the investigator if an eye exam has not been performed in the last 6 months. Note: If an eye examination has been performed no more than 6 months before screening, it will not have to be repeated; however, the investigator will need to confirm via interview that there is no change in subjective symptoms.

arms.name: Sequence A: LY900018 → IMG
arms.description: Participants receive 3 mg nasal LY900018 (single dose, intranasal) in Period 1, followed by 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (GlucaGen, single dose, IM injection) in Period 2, separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days

arms.name: Sequence B: IMG → LY900018
arms.description: Participants receive 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (GlucaGen, single dose, IM injection) in Period 1, followed by 3 mg nasal LY900018 (single dose, intranasal) in Period 2, separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days

objectives.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
objectives.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

endpoints.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
endpoints.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

objectives.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
objectives.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
endpoints.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
objectives.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
objectives.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

objectives.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
objectives.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

objectives.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
objectives.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

estimands.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients are excluded if the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, or if they receive an external measure to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods) Summary measure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration (beyond the first 10 minutes) to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; data collected after IV glucose infusion may be excluded from efficacy analysis

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, including adverse events, withdrawal of consent, or investigator decision

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable primary outcome due to insufficient hypoglycemia induction
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient's lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, indicating hypoglycemia was not sufficiently induced, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

estimands.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
estimands.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of study treatment, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements (Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts, incidence rates, and percentages of patients experiencing SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, summarized by treatment group; nasal/respiratory and anosmia AEs identified using preferred terms and summarized by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event prior to completing both treatment periods

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of concomitant medications for adverse event management
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications to manage treatment-emergent adverse events such as nausea, vomiting, or allergic reactions during the study period

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention to manage hypoglycemia during the study procedure, which may confound safety assessments

estimands.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PK samples collected during the study (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PK data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; comparative summary of PK parameters between LY900018 and IMG.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PK samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing, hemolyzed, or otherwise non-evaluable PK blood samples that prevent reliable estimation of one or more PK parameters

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia, which may affect glucagon PK measurements

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completion of the full 4-hour post-dose PK sampling schedule

estimands.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD (plasma glucose) samples collected during the study (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PD data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters by treatment group; comparative summary of PD parameters between LY900018 and IMG.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other external measure to raise PG concentration after glucagon administration; measurements taken after the time of intervention will be excluded from PD analysis

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PD plasma glucose samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or otherwise non-evaluable plasma glucose samples that prevent reliable estimation of one or more PD parameters

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PD sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completion of the full post-dose plasma glucose sampling schedule

estimands.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of LY900018 or IMG and have evaluable antibody samples collected at baseline and follow-up (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody data) Summary measure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group; frequency counts and percentages.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing follow-up antibody sample
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not attend the follow-up visit or does not provide an evaluable blood sample for anti-glucagon antibody assessment 26 to 30 days after last study treatment

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before follow-up antibody assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient withdraws consent or is lost to follow-up before the scheduled antibody assessment at the follow-up visit

estimands.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Recovery Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product and complete the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire at baseline and post-dose time points (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for baseline, post-dose time point values, and absolute change from baseline in total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other external measure to raise PG concentration, which may confound the assessment of hypoglycemia symptom recovery attributable to glucagon treatment

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not complete or partially completes the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire at one or more scheduled post-dose time points

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of symptom assessments
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completing all scheduled hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire assessments

Unless otherwise stated in subsections below, all samples collected for specified laboratory tests will be destroyed within 60 days of receipt of confirmed test results. Certain samples may be retained for a longer period, if necessary, to comply with applicable laws, regulations, or laboratory certification standards.
If a patient sneezes immediately after administration, document using the Nasal and Non-nasal Score Questionnaire (see Appendix 6 for a copy of the questionnaire).

Although all AEs are recorded in the CRF after signing informed consent, SAE reporting to the sponsor begins after the patient has signed informed consent and has received investigational product. However, if an SAE occurs after signing informed consent, but prior to receiving investigational product, AND is considered reasonably possibly related to a study procedure then it MUST be reported.

Pregnancy (maternal or paternal exposure to investigational product) does not meet the definition of an AE. However, to fulfill regulatory requirements any pregnancy should be reported following the SAE process to collect data on the outcome for both mother and fetus.

Nonserious AEs obtained through the questionnaire are recorded and analyzed separately. Only SAEs elicited through the Nasal and Non-nasal Score Questionnaire and Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale are to be recorded as AEs via CRF and reported to Lilly or its designee within 24 hours as SAEs.

For the purposes of this study, an overdose of LY900018 or IMG is considered any dose that is higher than the assigned dose. Refer to the LY900018 IB and GlucaGen Summary of Product Characteristics for more information.

Unscheduled orthostatic vital signs should be assessed, if possible, during any AE of dizziness or posture-induced symptoms. If orthostatic measurements are required, patients should be supine for at least 5 minutes and stand for at least 2 minutes. If the patient feels unable to stand, supine vital signs only will be recorded.
Single ECGs will be collected and stored locally at the investigator's site. Triplicate ECGs will be electronically transmitted to a central ECG laboratory designated by Lilly.
If an event of hypoglycemia falls into multiple subcategories, that event should only be counted once in the category of overall (or total) hypoglycemia.

Only severe hypoglycemic episodes will be reported separately as AEs. If a hypoglycemic event meets the criteria of severe, it needs to be recorded as serious in the CRF (that is, recorded as an SAE).

studyInterventions.name: LY900018
studyInterventions.description: Nasal glucagon powder formulation (3 mg) administered intranasally for rescue treatment of insulin-induced hypoglycemia

duration.text: Single administration per treatment period (2 periods total, separated by 3–14 day washout)
duration.reasonDurationWillVary: Single administration per treatment period (2 periods total, separated by 3–14 day washout)

studyInterventions.name: GlucaGen (intramuscular glucagon)
studyInterventions.description: Intramuscular glucagon (1 mg) administered by IM injection for rescue treatment of insulin-induced hypoglycemia; marketed product requiring reconstitution prior to administration

duration.text: Single administration per treatment period (2 periods total, separated by 3–14 day washout)
duration.reasonDurationWillVary: Single administration per treatment period (2 periods total, separated by 3–14 day washout)

studyInterventions.name: Human regular insulin (IV infusion)
studyInterventions.description: Diluted human regular insulin administered by IV infusion to induce hypoglycemia (target bedside PG <60 mg/dL) as part of the study procedure

administrations.name: Human regular insulin IV infusion for hypoglycemia induction

duration.text: Until bedside PG <60 mg/dL (maximum 4 hours); prepared as 0.3 U/mL by diluting 15 U human regular insulin [100 U/mL] into 50 mL saline
duration.reasonDurationWillVary: Until bedside PG <60 mg/dL (maximum 4 hours); prepared as 0.3 U/mL by diluting 15 U human regular insulin [100 U/mL] into 50 mL saline

administrations.description: Dose: 2 mU/kg/min (initial); up to 3 mU/kg/min (T1DM) or 4 mU/kg/min (T2DM); may be decreased to ~1.0 mU/kg/min when PG <90 mg/dL; Frequency: Continuous IV infusion until bedside PG <60 mg/dL

duration.text: As clinically required; given if PG <55 mg/dL at 30 min or <60 mg/dL at 45 min post glucagon dose, or if patient loses consciousness
duration.reasonDurationWillVary: As clinically required; given if PG <55 mg/dL at 30 min or <60 mg/dL at 45 min post glucagon dose, or if patient loses consciousness

studyInterventions.name: IV glucose
studyInterventions.description: Intravenous glucose administered if patient loses consciousness, PG declines too fast, or bedside PG remains <55 mg/dL at 30 minutes or <60 mg/dL at 45 minutes post glucagon dose

studyInterventions.name: Insulin (basal and prandial, patient's own regimen)
studyInterventions.description: Patients' stable anti-hyperglycemic insulin regimen (basal and/or prandial insulin analogs or CSII) continued throughout the study per protocol instructions on timing relative to the hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Oral anti-hyperglycemic medications (OAMs)
studyInterventions.description: Stable OAMs (metformin, DPP-4 inhibitor, SGLT2 inhibitor, sulfonylurea, glinides, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, thiazolidine) continued throughout the study per protocol instructions on timing

studyInterventions.name: Carbohydrate-rich meal
studyInterventions.description: Provided to all patients after completion of all PK blood sample collections at 240 minutes post glucagon dose before discharge from CRU
